archetypes.name: nit-marker-fidelity
archetypes.rationale: The plan prescribes two distinct nit-marker strings (`- **Severity**: nit` for design, `**Nit**` for implement) for counting accepted nits; if either doesn't match the actual rendered output the exclusion silently miscounts and the ≤5 bound applies to all accepted findings instead.
archetypes.prompt_body: Inspect the actual output files consumed by plan-review-loop.sh and review-and-fix.sh (`accepted-plan-findings.md` and round `findings.md`) to verify that the nit-counting patterns the plan prescribes exactly match what the reviewer renderers produce. Cross-reference `skills/shared/reviewer-templates.md` severity vocabulary with the existing `_count_important_findings` and `important_findings_present` grep patterns to determine whether the analogous nit helpers the plan proposes would also match in practice. If the markers differ — for example if the rendered line is `- **Severity**: Nit` (capitalized) or a different format than what the plan assumes — `NIT_ACCEPTED_COUNT` would be zero on every round, silently making nit findings count toward the ≤5 bound. Pin the exact marker strings in both loops against the reviewer template output format. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: kv-surface-completeness
archetypes.rationale: The plan removes `CONVERGENCE_STREAK` from KV emissions and adds `NIT_ACCEPTED_COUNT`/`NON_NIT_ACCEPTED_COUNT`; any parse site still expecting `CONVERGENCE_STREAK` or any exit path that never emits the new KVs creates a silent contract break.
archetypes.prompt_body: Search all scope files — SKILL.md Step 3 result-parsing case lists, test harnesses, and orchestration scripts — for every consume/parse site of `CONVERGENCE_STREAK` and confirm the plan explicitly covers each. Verify that `NIT_ACCEPTED_COUNT` and `NON_NIT_ACCEPTED_COUNT` are emitted on ALL exit paths of plan-review-loop.sh, not only the happy-path convergence: the snapshot-failure lookahead branch, the `cap-hit` terminal, `zero-findings` early exit, and `panel-failed` exit paths must all emit or explicitly omit these KVs without leaving downstream parsing in an undefined state. Confirm `write_step3_result_env` (line 165 area) emits the new KVs so that Step 3 result parsing in SKILL.md can consume them. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: part-c-reachability
archetypes.rationale: Part C (churn warning) in review-and-fix.sh calls `find_previous_non_degraded_round` to compare against a prior round; with single-round convergence now possible from round 1, Part C may have no prior round to reference, making its churn calculation incoherent or unreachable.
archetypes.prompt_body: Analyze the Part C churn-warning block in `skills/review-and-fix/scripts/review-and-fix.sh` (around lines 1407-1422) in light of the single-round convergence path the plan introduces. The plan preserves Part C unchanged but removes the two-round prerequisite that guaranteed a previous round existed when Part C fires. Determine whether Part C is reachable when the loop converges on round 1, whether `find_previous_non_degraded_round` returns a meaningful result with no prior round, and whether the churn delta calculation is guarded against the no-previous-round scenario. If Part C can silently produce a wrong or crash-inducing churn signal on round-1 convergence, the plan's 'KEEP unchanged' directive for Part C is incorrect and needs an explicit guard or reachability analysis. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
